t: This is St James the Less, a Church of England parish church in Pimlico, built between 1858 and 1861. It is Grade I listed, and has been described as one of the finest Gothic Revival churches anywhere. Look for the brick walls with touches of other stone, and the free-standing Italian-style tower, its most prominent outside feature. The architect was George Edmund Street, a leading Victorian Gothic Revival figure. Inside, he used design themes he had observed in medieval Gothic buildings across continental Europe. Street is best known for the Royal Courts of Justice on the Strand.
